abstract: Economists are increasingly concerned about a large but overlooked group of white-collar workers vulnerable to AI displacement, including customer service representatives, bookkeepers, payroll clerks, and human resources specialists. These back-office workers, while individually less visible than other professionals, collectively represent tens of millions of jobs at risk from automation.
keyFindings: A large group of white-collar back-office workers—customer service representatives, bookkeepers, payroll clerks, and human resources specialists—are particularly vulnerable to AI displacement
These at-risk workers collectively account for tens of millions of jobs despite receiving less public attention than higher-profile professions
